extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers/evaluators for DFG Emmy Noether Programme grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for external reviewers assessing applications to the DFG Emmy Noether Programme, covering applicant qualifications, project quality, work programme, host institution(s), budget, and special requests. The review should be concise (max two pages) and address whether the proposal should be approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review length
rubrics_metrics.description: The review should not exceed two pages in length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep evaluations concise and focused; adhere to the two-page maximum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programme objectives / fit with Emmy Noether Programme
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider that the programme enables highly qualified researchers in early career phases to become eligible for a university teaching career within a continuous period of six years and offers an alternative to habilitation by leading an independent junior research group. The programme also aims to encourage outstanding early-career researchers currently working abroad to enter or re-enter the German research system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how well the applicant and project align with the programme's goals (career trajectory toward professorship, suitability of the independent junior research group model, and potential to attract researchers from abroad). See the Guidelines for the Emmy Noether Programme (DFG form 50.02) for more context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness of preliminary work, publication quality, and applicant qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: How would you evaluate the soundness of the preliminary work, the quality of publications (please refer to the Guidelines for Publication Lists) and the qualifications of the applicant – both in general and in terms of the proposed project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on the applicant's track record, the relevance and quality of publications, and whether preliminary results/supporting work demonstrate feasibility. Relate publications to the project's aims using the Guidelines for Publication Lists as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to lead an independent junior research group and career prospects
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the applicant have the ability to independently lead a junior research group? How would you assess the applicant’s chances of being appointed to a professorship after the independent junior research group ends?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate leadership, management, mentoring potential, independence of research, and likelihood that the candidate will achieve a professorial appointment within/after the programme period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the project: originality and contribution to knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: How would you assess the quality of the project, especially with regard to originality and the anticipated contribution to knowledge?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess novelty, significance, and the expected impact of the research on the field. Discuss whether the project advances knowledge beyond the state of the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives and work programme (hypotheses, topic distinctness, strengths/weaknesses)
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent do the objectives and work programme convincingly reflect clear working hypotheses and an appropriately distinct topic? Please comment on the strengths and weaknesses of the planned investigations, the suitability of the methods and the appropriateness of the schedule. How do you rate the explanations on the handling of research data?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clarity and testability of hypotheses, focus and distinctness of the topic, methodological rigor, feasibility of the timeline, and adequacy of research data management (handling, storage, availability). Identify major risks and weaknesses and suggest improvements where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work and research environment / host institution suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: How would you assess the work and research environment? Is the host institution suitable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on institutional resources, infrastructure, supervisory/support environment, and whether the host can realistically support an independent junior research group. Consider institutional commitment and local conditions necessary for project success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple host institutions — evaluate all listed
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants in the Emmy Noether Programme have the option of naming more than one potential host institution in the proposal. A final decision does not have to be made until after the proposal is approved. Therefore, please comment on all institutions listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess each listed institution's suitability and note any differences in support, infrastructure, or fit with the project that may affect selection or implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation on approval and budget justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Please provide a clear recommendation as to whether the proposal should be approved. If so, comment on whether the requested funds are justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed project, making recommendations for adjustments to the budget as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give a clear, actionable recommendation (approve/reject/conditional). Evaluate the realism and necessity of the requested budget items, flag overspending or missing resources, and propose specific adjustments if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for specialised literature
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposal involves requests for specialised literature, note: Funds for purchasing specialised scientific publications may be granted in exceptional cases where the publications in question must either be permanently available to the project but are not purchased by the institution, or when they are not available through interlibrary loan. State explicitly whether you believe the funds for procuring the specialised literature listed in the proposal should be approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether each requested specialised publication meets the exceptional criteria (permanent need not met by institution, unavailable via interlibrary loan). Provide explicit approval/non-approval recommendation for those literature requests.
